units.text: INT. BARBARA - CONTINUOUS
I can see you are my eldest. I am very glad to meet you again, my boy.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: LOMAX [remonstrating] No but look here don't you know--[Overcome] Oh I say!
LADY BRITOMART [recovering from momentary speechlessness] Andrew: do you mean to say that you don't remember how many children you have?
Well, I am afraid I--. They have grown so much--er. Am I making any ridiculous mistake? I may as well confess: I recollect only one son. But so many things have happened since, of course--er--
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: LADY BRITOMART [decisively] Andrew: you are talking nonsense.
Of course you have only one son.
Perhaps you will be good enough to introduce me, my dear.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: That is Charles Lomax, who is engaged to Sarah.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: My dear sir, I beg your pardon.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: Not at all. Delighted, I assure you.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: This is Stephen.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: UNDERSHAFT [bowing] Happy to make your acquaintance, Mr Stephen.
Then [going to Cusins] you must be my son. [Taking Cusins' hands in his] How are you, my young friend? [To Lady Britomart] He is very like you, my love.
You flatter me, Mr Undershaft. My name is Cusins: engaged to Barbara.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Very explicitly.
That is Major Barbara Undershaft, of the Salvation Army. That is Sarah, your second daughter. This is Stephen Undershaft, your son.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: My dear Stephen, I beg your pardon.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: Not at all.
units.name: STEPHEN

units.text: Mr Cusins: I am much indebted to you for explaining so precisely.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: Turning to Sarah.
Barbara, my dear--
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: SARAH [prompting him] Sarah.
Sarah, of course.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: They shake hands.
He goes over to Barbara.
Barbara--I am right this time, I hope.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: Quite right.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: They shake hands.
LADY BRITOMART [resuming command] Sit down, all of you.
Sit down, Andrew. [She comes forward and sits on the settle.
Cusins also brings his chair forward on her left.
Barbara and Stephen resume their seats.
Lomax gives his chair to Sarah and goes for another].
Thank you, my love.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: LOMAX [conversationally, as he brings a chair forward between the writing table and the settee, and offers it to Undershaft] Takes you some time to find out exactly where you are, don't it?
UNDERSHAFT [accepting the chair] That is not what embarrasses me, Mr Lomax.
My difficulty is that if I play the part of a father, I shall produce the effect of an intrusive stranger; and if I play the part of a discreet stranger, I may appear a callous father.
There is no need for you to play any part at all, Andrew. You had much better be sincere and natural.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: UNDERSHAFT [submissively] Yes, my dear: I daresay that will be best. [Making himself comfortable] Well, here I am.
Now what can I do for you all?
You need not do anything, Andrew. You are one of the family. You can sit with us and enjoy yourself.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: Lomax's too long suppressed mirth explodes in agonized neighings.
LADY BRITOMART [outraged] Charles Lomax: if you can behave yourself, behave yourself.
If not, leave the room.
I'm awfully sorry, Lady Brit; but really, you know, upon my soul!
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: He sits on the settee between Lady Britomart and Undershaft, quite overcome.
Why don't you laugh if you want to, Cholly? It's good for your inside.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: Barbara: you have had the education of a lady. Please let your father see that; and don't talk like a street girl.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: Never mind me, my dear. As you know, I am not a gentleman; and I was never educated.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: LOMAX [encouragingly] Nobody'd know it, I assure you.
You look all right, you know.

Let me advise you to study Greek, Mr Undershaft. Greek scholars are privileged men. Few of them know Greek; and none of them know anything else; but their position is unchallengeable. Other languages are the qualifications of waiters and commercial travellers: Greek is to a man of position what the hallmark is to silver.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Dolly: don't be insincere. Cholly: fetch your concertina and play something for us.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: LOMAX [doubtfully to Undershaft] Perhaps that sort of thing isn't in your line, eh?
I am particularly fond of music.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: LOMAX [delighted] Are you?
Then I'll get it. [He goes upstairs for the instrument].
